quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?

options.text: Eyeglasses
Sunglasses
A windshield
Goggles

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Alcohol starts to impair your riding at:

options.text: Well below the legal limit.
Once reaching the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking any alcohol. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: You should normally keep a following distance of:

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance in bad weather or poor conditions.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have a difficult time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and use your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see traffic around you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Other drivers should:

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle at any time.
Share a lane with a motorcycle during heavy traffic.
Share a lane with a motorcycle when merging onto a highway.
Never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Both motorcycles and cars need a full lane to operate safely. Lane sharing is usually not allowed.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Kick it away.
Stop until the animal loses interest.
Swerve around the animal.
Approach slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased, downshift and approach the dog slowly. Then accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount the motorcycle only after the engine has started. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt firmly. Their feet must stay on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Wear dark-colored clothing.
Wear bright-colored clothing.
Do not ride during the day.
Choose safer routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself more visible. This reduces your crash risk, even during the day.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you slow down where other drivers do not expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you slow down where other drivers do not expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, such as the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: When you ride beside another vehicle, the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The other vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Change your lane position and adjust to the conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position and adjust to the conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about where you position your motorcycle in your lane, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From the motorcycle's former owner.
From the owner's manual.
From a library book about motorcycles.
From a motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle. Always read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in foggy conditions. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Speed up.
Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up only makes the situation more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: How should you position your motorcycle to see better before passing a vehicle on its left?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Ride in the center portion of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane before passing. This improves your view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Engine braking is when you shift to a lower gear to slow down. It works the same way as using your brakes.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's stopping distance?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars need about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars need about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes it much harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: Your lane position should help you:

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop others from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Good lane position protects your space and shows other drivers what you intend to do.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride side-by-side.
Use both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: When riding curves, turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway, riders should switch to single-file formation. Staggered formation is normally used, but not in these situations.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close together while keeping safe distance is to ride:

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping safe space around each rider. Switch to single-file when riding curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Do not need space cushions.
Should increase their space cushions.
Should cut their usual space cushions in half.
Should keep adequate space cushions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep adequate space cushions.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, stay close together but always keep safe space around each rider.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow-moving cars, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic moves.
Ride on the shoulder to pass through quickly.
Weave between cars to pass through quickly.
Not weave between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between cars.
questions.explanation: Weaving between slow or stopped cars is dangerous. Car doors can open or cars may suddenly move into traffic. You won't have room to react safely. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.
